name: sol_basics_function_9
description: Missing access control on sensitive state-changing function
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that changes contract state or performs a sensitive operation (e.g., minting, burning, transferring funds, changing thresholds, or acting on behalf of another user) without any access-control check (such as an onlyOwner/onlyAdmin modifier or a caller-identity/authorization check), allowing an arbitrary or unauthorized caller to invoke it and cause unintended state changes or loss of funds; this excludes functions intentionally open to any caller by design (e.g., public view functions, permissionless deposits) and functions that already enforce a modifier or explicit require-based caller check.
criteria: A mint or burn function transfers or creates tokens based on caller-supplied parameters with no modifier or require statement restricting who can call it
A function that changes a critical protocol parameter (e.g., approval threshold, rebalancer address, fee rate) can be called by any external address with no ownership or role check
A function that initiates a loan, withdrawal, or transfer on behalf of another user's collateral/funds does not verify that msg.sender is the owner or an approved delegate
A privileged administrative function (e.g., pause, upgrade, set config) is declared public/external and lacks any onlyOwner/onlyAdmin modifier or equivalent authorization check
